I asked him how much is going to be, he goes, it's between 1 and 6'. NOTE FOR THE CENTRAL BUILD, NOT A CLAIM: the corpus lists an unidentified setter code 'DH'. prospect.name: Vimal
prospect.occupation: Business owner/executive — 'the business that I'm involved in, we have operations in UK, Europe, South Africa' and 'we employ quite a lot of people'. Office-based with substantial international travel.
prospect.family_status: Two young children — daughter Amelia, 8, and a son, 4. Puts them to bed before his evening meal.
prospect.training_background: Twenty-plus years of consistent weight training, self-described as non-professional bodybuilding style with push/pull splits and rotating body parts. Trains every single day: roughly three days weights, three days boxing (bag, pads, light sparring, no competitive fighting), and a 20-25 km cycle on Sundays. Takes 5 g creatine daily and protein shakes. Very strong in fixed planes — leg presses 300 kg — but limited in free movement. Has tried a kettlebell once. Started meditating during COVID.
prospect.medical: No formal conditions disclosed and none asked about. Self-reported musculoskeletal picture: restricted hip mobility which he attributes to long hours seated, and which he says presents as 'weak lower back, weak glutes, maybe a bit of knee pain'. Cannot squat deep with a free bar and keeps it 'really light' as a result. References occasionally pulling something in his back. States there are 'no day-to-day issues'. Sleeps a solid seven hours, wakes rested. Current weight 84 kg targeting 78 kg (recorded above in lb as 185). NOTE: no injury, health-condition or clearance question was asked at any point, and the rep recommended replacing his entire strength programme.

objections.raw_quote: No, I will digest because I didn't know what the price was going to be. ... So let me take that away. Let me at least consider it for a day and then I can come back
objections.rep_response: Worked it properly and in the right order. Isolated finances first — 'let's put finances aside. Like does this kind of check all the boxes for you?' — then ran the belief question, then checked for anything hidden ('apart from the finances is there anything else'), then asked the direct budget question, then 'So what's stopping you to actually start now?'. He also tried a mild guilt variant, 'I thought you are committed', which the prospect corrected cleanly. None of the OA decision-frame moves ran.

objections.rep_response: Not addressed at all. The prospect half-answered it himself ('But also, this is something different, right? If I was going to just pay for a personal trainer, I would have done it') and the rep moved straight on to 'So what's stopping you to actually start now?'. The comparison to a UK personal trainer was left standing unchallenged.

objections.raw_quote: Even if it was two grand, I think that's not the point. This is a commitment over six months, which is my second call today, so I wouldn't just be impulsively just saying yes. I would be making sure, how do I make decisions? I make decisions by taking all the information, digesting, and making a decision, and then progressing.
objections.rep_response: Accepted it without challenge and moved to logistics, agreeing a 24-hour decision window and exchanging WhatsApp numbers. This is arguably the correct read of the prospect, but it means the call ended with no mechanism holding the decision — no deposit, no start date, no expiry.

objections.raw_quote: how does it work in terms of ensuring I'm doing things properly? Because lifting weights is relatively easy ... With this, where do my concerns come from? Which is, have I got the right form to be able to doing this properly?
objections.rep_response: Deferred it deliberately to the accountability section ('I'll get into that bit after nutrition, okay?') and then answered it with the video-feedback mechanism — record on the phone, send via app, receive video correction from Trevor. The prospect confirmed it landed: 'It covers my question from earlier.'

objections.raw_quote: my only other thing would be, would this training, if it's replacing the current strength component of my training, would it still allow me to maintain a level of strength?
objections.rep_response: Answered with reassurance and mechanism rather than evidence — bodyweight work would be included (pull-ups, dips, push-ups) and he would progress from a starting bell. 'Absolutely... So you're going to be good, believe me.' No data, no case example and no acknowledgement that a man who leg presses 300 kg being started on a 16 kg bell is a legitimate concern.

outcome.next_step: Prospect to make a decision within 24 hours and message the rep on WhatsApp at approximately the same time the following day. If yes, the rep hands to a team member for onboarding. Rep travelling from the next day, back 10 August.

notable.note: Two findings worth escalating. First, the setter gave this prospect a price range of 'between 1 and 6' the day before — 'he goes, it's between 1 and 6, but he goes, the next call will tell you more. So it's come out at 6.' A setter quoting a range that starts at $1,000 primes every prospect to expect a tier six times cheaper than the real price, and it lands the closer at the top of a range instead of at a single number. Read alongside the improvised $3,000 tier on the smanian call the same day, there is a real question about what price points are actually being represented to the market. Second, the rep undercut physiotherapy advice unprompted — 'when they go to a PT, they say, oh, you need to stretch... but when your muscles are going to be weak, your stretching doesn't help you like at all' — to a prospect presenting with hip restriction, weak glutes and knee pain who has never been clinically assessed. On process this is otherwise one of the better calls in the batch: the baseline was genuinely thorough, the bigger-why question was asked verbatim, and the commitment check ran properly before price.

quality.notes: Severe and sustained inversion. For long stretches the labels are simply reversed: 'So nutrition, could you just briefly walk me through, like, what exactly are you eating on a daily basis?' at 00:09:13 is labelled Vimal but is the rep, and the entire weight exchange at 00:06:41 ('Right now you're 84 kilos, right?' / 'And you want to hit 78') is split across the wrong speakers. The final objection sequence from roughly 00:44:17 to 00:47:23 runs as a single unpunctuated block with both speakers merged, including the critical 'is this 6k within your budget' question and its answer. Roles assigned entirely from content.
